paragraphs.text: בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים וְחָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנָ֣ה לְ֠גָלוּתֵנוּ בְּרֹ֨אשׁ הַשָּׁנָ֜ה בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר בְּעֶ֣צֶם ׀ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד־יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck — on that very day the hand of YHWH was upon me, and he brought me there.

notes.official: The date is the twenty-fifth year of the exile (of 597), 'at the beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month', the fourteenth year after the fall of the city: 573 BCE. *bərōʾš haššānâ* 'at the beginning of the year' occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and is rendered literally. It may mean the spring (Nisan) or the autumn (Tishri) new year, and later Jewish usage made it the name of the autumn festival. Commentators note that the tenth day of the seventh month is the day the jubilee is proclaimed (Lev 25:9), and that the twenty-fifth year is half a jubilee (Zimmerli, *Ezekiel 2*, Hermeneia). *hāyəṯâ ʿālay yaḏ-YHWH* 'the hand of YHWH was upon me' (`yad-yhwh`).

paragraphs.text: בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים הֱבִיאַ֖נִי אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי אֶל־הַ֤ר גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְעָלָ֥יו כְּמִבְנֵה־עִ֖יר מִנֶּֽגֶב׃

i18n.en: In visions of Elohim he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, and on it was something like the structure of a city, on the south.

notes.official:
*bəmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm* 'in visions of Elohim' (`mar'ot-elohim`), as at 1:1 and 8:3. *ʾel-ʾereṣ yiśrāʾēl* 'to the land of Israel' (`eretz`). *ʾel-har gāḇōah məʾōḏ* 'on a very high mountain', the mountain of Zion raised up as in 17:22-23, 20:40 and Isa 2:2.

*wəʿālāyw kəmiḇnēh-ʿîr minneḡeḇ* 'and on it was something like the structure of a city, on the south'. The MT has *ʿālāyw* 'on it'; the LXX reads 'opposite' (*apenanti*, Hebrew *neḡeḏ*). The MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *miḇneh* is 'structure, building' (ASV 'as it were the frame of a city'), and the comparative *kə-* ('something like') is the Hebrew's.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes 40:2-3 ('set me down upon a very high mountain, by which was as the frame of a city on the south ... a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass'). It reads the city as one of the creators' terrestrial bases on high mountains. The line renders the verse lexically and keeps the Hebrew's 'something like'.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ מַרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וּפְתִיל־פִּשְׁתִּ֥ים בְּיָד֖וֹ וּקְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֑ה וְה֥וּא עֹמֵ֖ד בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃

i18n.en: He brought me there, and behold — a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a cord of flax in his hand and the measuring reed; and he was standing in the gate.

notes.official:
*wəhinnēh-ʾîš marʾēhû kəmarʾēh nəḥōšeṯ* 'and behold — a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze'. *nəḥōšeṯ* is copper or bronze. 'Bronze' is the book's rendering (1:7 'burnished bronze'; cf. Dan 10:6); the ASV 'brass' is the older English for the same alloy. The appearance formula is kept (`mar'eh-demut`).

*ûp̄əṯîl-pištîm bəyāḏô ûqənēh hammiddâ* 'with a cord of flax in his hand and the measuring reed': the cord measures long distances (cf. 47:3) and the reed short ones (`measures-cubit-handbreadth-span-reed-ezekiel`). *pištîm* is the flax plant and its fibre; the same word is rendered 'linen' at 44:17-18, where it names cloth. The English uses the word that suits each object, as the ASV does.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) reads the man 'whose appearance was like the appearance of brass' as a figure wearing a metallic suit. The line keeps the Hebrew simile ('like the appearance of bronze') unchanged.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֵלַ֜י הָאִ֗ישׁ בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם רְאֵ֣ה בְעֵינֶיךָ֩ וּבְאָזְנֶ֨יךָ שְּׁמָ֜ע וְשִׂ֣ים לִבְּךָ֗ לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִי֙ מַרְאֶ֣ה אוֹתָ֔ךְ כִּ֛י לְמַ֥עַן הַרְאוֹתְכָ֖ה הֻבָ֣אתָה הֵ֑נָּה הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: The man said to me, "Son of human, see with your eyes and hear with your ears, and set your heart on all that I am showing you; for you have been brought here in order that I may show it to you. Declare all that you see to the house of Israel."

notes.official: *rəʾēh ḇəʿênêḵā ûḇəʾāzəneḵā šəmāʿ wəśîm libbəḵā* 'see with your eyes and hear with your ears, and set your heart': *śîm lēḇ* is kept literally, as at 44:5. *haggēḏ ʾeṯ-kol-ʾăšer-ʾattâ rōʾeh ləḇêṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'declare all that you see to the house of Israel' (cf. 43:10-11). The speech is a single verse.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֥ה חוֹמָ֛ה מִח֥וּץ לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב וּבְיַ֨ד הָאִ֜ישׁ קְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֗ה שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֤וֹת בָּֽאַמָּה֙ וָטֹ֔פַח וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־רֹ֤חַב הַבִּנְיָן֙ קָנֶ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וְקוֹמָ֖ה קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: And behold — a wall outside the house, all around; and in the man's hand the measuring reed, six cubits long, each cubit a cubit and a handbreadth; and he measured the thickness of the building, one reed, and the height, one reed.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh ḥômâ miḥûṣ labbayiṯ sāḇîḇ sāḇîḇ* 'And behold — a wall outside the house, all around'. *qənēh hammiddâ šēš-ʾammôṯ bāʾammâ wāṭōp̄aḥ* 'the measuring reed, six cubits long, each cubit a cubit and a handbreadth'. This is the long cubit of seven handbreadths, about 52 cm, as against the common cubit of six, about 45 cm (cf. 43:13; 2 Chr 3:3 'cubits of the old measure'). The reed is therefore about 3.1 m. Units stay in their ancient form, numbers are written out, and conversions are given only here in the commentary (`measures-cubit-handbreadth-span-reed-ezekiel`). *rōḥaḇ habbinyān* 'the thickness of the building' is the thickness of the wall (ASV).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל־שַׁ֙עַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנָיו֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֔ימָה וַיַּ֖עַל במעלותו [בְּמַֽעֲלוֹתָ֑יו] וַיָּ֣מָד ׀ אֶת־סַ֣ף הַשַּׁ֗עַר קָנֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ רֹ֔חַב וְאֵת֙ סַ֣ף אֶחָ֔ד קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד רֹֽחַב׃

i18n.en: Then he came to the gate whose face was toward the east, and went up its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate, one reed wide, and the one threshold, one reed wide.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *bmʿlwtw* / Qere *bəmaʿălôṯāyw* 'its steps'. The Ketiv *-w* is the older spelling of the plural suffix *-āyw*; there is no change of sense (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). The same pattern recurs throughout 40:9-37.

*wəʾēṯ sap̄ ʾeḥāḏ qāneh ʾeḥāḏ rōḥaḇ* 'and the one threshold, one reed wide' repeats the measurement just given. It is absent in the LXX and probably a dittography; the ASV smooths it as 'the other threshold'. The MT is translated as it stands (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַתָּ֗א קָנֶ֨ה אֶחָ֥ד אֹ֙רֶךְ֙ וְקָנֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ רֹ֔חַב וּבֵ֥ין הַתָּאִ֖ים חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וְסַ֣ף הַ֠שַּׁעַר מֵאֵ֨צֶל אוּלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֛עַר מֵֽהַבַּ֖יִת קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: And the guardroom was one reed long and one reed wide; and between the guardrooms, five cubits; and the threshold of the gate beside the porch of the gate, toward the house, one reed.

notes.official:
*wəhattāʾ qāneh ʾeḥāḏ ʾōreḵ* 'And the guardroom was one reed long'. *tāʾ* is a chamber opening off the gate passage; outside Ezek 40 it occurs only for the guardroom of the royal runners at 1 Kgs 14:28 // 2 Chr 12:11 (BDB 'guard-chamber'; HALOT 'guardroom'). The ASV 'lodge' suggests a separate building to a modern reader, so 'guardroom' is used (`ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`). Three such rooms on each side of the passage (v 10) correspond to the 'six-chamber' city gates excavated at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer (Yadin, *IEJ* 8, 1958), a parallel commentators have long noted (Zimmerli; Block, *Ezekiel 25-48*, NICOT).

*sap̄* 'threshold'. *ʾûlām haššaʿar* 'the porch of the gate' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`: *ʾûlām* 'porch').

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־אֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֛עַר מֵהַבַּ֖יִת קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: He measured the porch of the gate toward the house, one reed.

notes.official: The verse repeats 40:9a with a different measurement and is absent in the LXX, Syriac, Vulgate and many Hebrew manuscripts; most explain it as a dittography. It is MT and is translated in full, without smoothing (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *ʾûlām* 'porch' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־אֻלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה אַמּ֔וֹת ואילו [וְאֵילָ֖יו] שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֑וֹת וְאֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֖עַר מֵהַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: He measured the porch of the gate, eight cubits, and its posts, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was toward the house.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *wʾylw* / Qere *wəʾêlāyw* 'and its posts' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *ʾayil* (plural *ʾêlîm*) is the architectural *ʾayil*: a pier or pilaster projecting from the wall at the passage and porch. It is a homonym of *ʾayil* 'ram' (43:23, 25). The ASV 'post(s)' is kept; modern versions have 'jambs' or 'pilasters' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`). *ʾûlām haššaʿar* 'the porch of the gate' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְתָאֵ֨י הַשַּׁ֜עַר דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֗ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה מִפֹּה֙ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה מִפֹּ֔ה מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּ֑ם וּמִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לָאֵילִ֖ם מִפֹּ֥ה וּמִפּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the guardrooms of the gate toward the east were three on this side and three on that side; one measure for the three of them, and one measure for the posts on this side and on that side.

notes.official: *wətāʾê haššaʿar ... šəlōšâ mippōh ûšəlōšâ mippōh* 'the guardrooms of the gate ... three on this side and three on that side' (`ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`): the six-chamber plan (see 40:7). *ʾêlîm* 'posts' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֛מָד אֶת־רֹ֥חַב פֶּֽתַח־הַשַּׁ֖עַר עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֑וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר שְׁל֥וֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה אַמּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: He measured the width of the opening of the gate, ten cubits; the length of the gate, thirteen cubits.

notes.official: *rōḥaḇ peṯaḥ-haššaʿar ʿeśer ʾammôṯ ʾōreḵ haššaʿar šəlôš ʿeśrēh ʾammôṯ* 'the width of the opening of the gate, ten cubits; the length of the gate, thirteen cubits'. The second figure cannot be a length, since the gate is fifty cubits long (v 15). It is usually taken as the width of the passage, or of the doorway including its jambs (Zimmerli). The Hebrew 'length' is kept.

paragraphs.text: וּגְב֞וּל לִפְנֵ֤י הַתָּאוֹת֙ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאַמָּה־אַחַ֥ת גְּב֖וּל מִפֹּ֑ה וְהַתָּ֕א שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֣וֹת מִפּ֔וֹ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And a border in front of the guardrooms, one cubit, and a border of one cubit on that side; and the guardroom, six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.

notes.official: *ûḡəḇûl lip̄nê hattāʾôṯ ʾammâ ʾeḥāṯ* 'And a border in front of the guardrooms, one cubit': *gəḇûl* is a barrier or kerb, the word used for Israel's 'border' at 11:10-11 and for the altar's 'border' at 43:13, 17. *wəhattāʾ* 'and the guardroom' (`ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣מָד אֶת־הַשַּׁ֗עַר מִגַּ֤ג הַתָּא֙ לְגַגּ֔וֹ רֹ֕חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת פֶּ֖תַח נֶ֥גֶד פָּֽתַח׃

i18n.en: He measured the gate from the roof of the one guardroom to the roof of the other, a width of twenty-five cubits, entrance opposite entrance.

notes.official: *miggaḡ hattāʾ ləḡaggô* 'from the roof of the one guardroom to the roof of the other' (`ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`). The LXX reads 'from wall to wall', and the 'roof' is often explained as the top of the back walls. *peṯaḥ neḡeḏ pāṯaḥ* 'entrance opposite entrance': the doors of facing rooms are aligned.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־אֵילִ֖ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וְאֶל־אֵיל֙ הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר הַשַּׁ֖עַר סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: He made posts, sixty cubits; and to the post of the court, the gate all around.

notes.official: *wayyaʿaś ʾeṯ-ʾêlîm šiššîm ʾammâ wəʾel-ʾêl heḥāṣēr haššaʿar sāḇîḇ sāḇîḇ* is one of the most obscure verses of the vision. 'He made posts, sixty cubits' gives no measure that fits the plan, and the LXX has a different text. The line renders the MT literally, without the ASV's supplied '[reached]', and the obscurity is recorded here rather than resolved (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וְעַ֗ל פְּנֵי֙ הַשַּׁ֣עַר היאתון [הָֽאִית֔וֹן] עַל־לִפְנֵ֕י אֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֖עַר הַפְּנִימִ֑י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And from the front of the gate at the entrance to the front of the inner porch of the gate, fifty cubits.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *hyʾtwn* / Qere *hāʾîṯôn* 'the entrance'. The noun occurs only here and is formed from *ʾth* 'come' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). The fifty cubits are the full length of the gate-building from the outer face to the inner porch (cf. vv 21, 25, 29, 33, 36). *ʾûlām* 'porch' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְחַלֹּנ֣וֹת אֲטֻמ֣וֹת אֶֽל־הַתָּאִ֡ים וְאֶל֩ אֵלֵיהֵ֨מָה לִפְנִ֤ימָה לַשַּׁ֙עַר֙ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֔יב וְכֵ֖ן לָאֵֽלַמּ֑וֹת וְחַלּוֹנ֞וֹת סָבִ֤יב ׀ סָבִיב֙ לִפְנִ֔ימָה וְאֶל־אַ֖יִל תִּמֹרִֽים׃

i18n.en: And there were closed windows toward the guardrooms and toward their posts, inward to the gate all around, and likewise for the vestibules; and windows all around inward; and on the post, palm-trees.

notes.official:
*wəḥallōnôṯ ʾăṭumôṯ* 'closed windows': *ʾāṭam* is 'stop up, close' (Prov 21:13). The windows are fixed or latticed, like the *ḥallônê šəqup̄îm ʾăṭumîm* of the Solomonic Temple (1 Kgs 6:4, kings-woh 'windows of fixed lattice-work'); NRSV has 'recessed windows'. *ʾel-hattāʾîm* 'toward the guardrooms' (`ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`); *ʾêlêhēmmâ* 'their posts' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`).

*wəḵēn lāʾēlammôṯ* 'and likewise for the vestibules'. *ʾêlām* (plural *ʾêlammôṯ*) is usually explained as a by-form of *ʾûlām* 'porch' (BDB; HALOT), here the vestibule of the gate. The KJV/ASV 'arches' has no lexical support. The line uses 'vestibule(s)' so the reader can still see the separate spelling, while central *ʾûlām* stays 'porch' (`elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`). *tîmōrîm* 'palm-trees', the carved palm ornaments of 1 Kgs 6:29.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה לְשָׁכוֹת֙ וְרִֽצְפָ֔ה עָשׂ֥וּי לֶחָצֵ֖ר סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים לְשָׁכ֖וֹת אֶל־הָרִֽצְפָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me into the outer court, and behold — chambers and a pavement made for the court all around; thirty chambers upon the pavement.

notes.official: *ləšāḵôṯ wəriṣp̄â* 'chambers and a pavement': *riṣp̄â* is a stone pavement (2 Chr 7:3; Esth 1:6). The thirty chambers along the outer court are the rooms for communal meals (cf. Jer 35:2-4).

paragraphs.text: וְהָרִֽצְפָה֙ אֶל־כֶּ֣תֶף הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לְעֻמַּ֖ת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים הָרִֽצְפָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the pavement was beside the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates — the lower pavement.

notes.official: *hāriṣp̄â hattaḥtônâ* 'the lower pavement': the outer court lies below the inner, which is reached by eight steps (40:31, 34, 37).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣מָד רֹ֡חַב מִלִּפְנֵי֩ הַשַּׁ֨עַר הַתַּחְתּ֜וֹנָה לִפְנֵ֨י הֶחָצֵ֧ר הַפְּנִימִ֛י מִח֖וּץ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה הַקָּדִ֖ים וְהַצָּפֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: He measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court outside, a hundred cubits, on the east and on the north.

notes.official: *mē'ah ʾammâ haqqāḏîm wəhaṣṣāp̄ôn* 'a hundred cubits, on the east and on the north': the elliptical phrase means that the distance was measured on both sides (east and north) and found the same.

paragraphs.text: וְהַשַּׁ֗עַר אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנָיו֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן לֶחָצֵ֖ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֑ה מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the gate whose face was toward the north, belonging to the outer court — he measured its length and its width.

notes.official: *wəhaššaʿar ʾăšer pānāyw dereḵ haṣṣāp̄ôn* 'And the gate whose face was toward the north'. The measuring of the north and south outer gates (vv 20-27) follows the pattern of the east gate.

paragraphs.text: ותאו [וְתָאָ֗יו] שְׁלוֹשָׁ֤ה מִפּוֹ֙ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה מִפּ֔וֹ ואילו [וְאֵילָ֤יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙] הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים בָּאַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And its guardrooms, three on this side and three on that side, and its posts and its vestibules were according to the measure of the first gate: its length fifty cubits, and the width twenty-five cubits.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, three readings: Ketiv *wtʾw* / Qere *wəṯāʾāyw* 'and its guardrooms'; Ketiv *wʾylw* / Qere *wəʾêlāyw* 'and its posts'; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules'. All are defective spellings of the plural suffix (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). For the terms see `ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`, `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40` and `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`. *ḥămiššîm ʾammâ* 'fifty cubits', the length of the gate as at v 15. *ḥāmēš wəʿeśrîm bāʾammâ* is literally 'twenty-five by the cubit', rendered 'twenty-five cubits'.

paragraphs.text: וחלונו [וְחַלּוֹנָ֤יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙] ותמרו [וְתִ֣מֹרָ֔יו] כְּמִדַּ֣ת הַשַּׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וּבְמַעֲל֥וֹת שֶׁ֙בַע֙ יַֽעֲלוּ־ב֔וֹ ואילמו [וְאֵֽילַמָּ֖יו] לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And its windows and its vestibules and its palm-trees were according to the measure of the gate whose face was toward the east; and by seven steps they would go up into it, and its vestibules were before them.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, four readings: Ketiv *wḥlwnw* / Qere *wəḥallônāyw* 'and its windows'; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules'; Ketiv *wtmrw* / Qere *wəṯimōrāyw* 'and its palm-trees'; Ketiv *wʾylmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`). *ûḇəmaʿălôṯ šeḇaʿ yaʿălû-ḇô* 'by seven steps they would go up into it': the outer gates have seven steps and the inner gates eight (vv 31, 34, 37).

paragraphs.text: וְשַׁ֙עַר֙ לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔י נֶ֣גֶד הַשַּׁ֔עַר לַצָּפ֖וֹן וְלַקָּדִ֑ים וַיָּ֧מָד מִשַּׁ֛עַר אֶל־שַׁ֖עַר מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And there was a gate to the inner court opposite the gate, on the north and on the east; and he measured from gate to gate, a hundred cubits.

notes.official: *wəšaʿar leḥāṣēr happənîmî neḡeḏ haššaʿar* 'And there was a gate to the inner court opposite the gate': each outer gate faces an inner gate across the outer court, a hundred cubits apart.

paragraphs.text: וַיּוֹלִכֵ֙נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה־שַׁ֖עַר דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֑וֹם וּמָדַ֤ד אילו [אֵילָיו֙] ואילמו [וְאֵ֣ילַמָּ֔יו] כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: Then he led me toward the south, and behold — a gate toward the south; and he measured its posts and its vestibules according to these measures.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *ʾylw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw* 'its posts'; Ketiv *wʾylmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וְחַלּוֹנִ֨ים ל֤וֹ ולאילמו [וּלְאֵֽילַמָּיו֙] סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֔יב כְּהַחֲלֹּנ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And there were windows in it and in its vestibules all around, like these windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *wlʾylmw* / Qere *ûləʾêlammāyw* 'and in its vestibules' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וּמַעֲל֤וֹת שִׁבְעָה֙ עלותו [עֹֽלוֹתָ֔יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּ֖יו] לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְתִמֹרִ֣ים ל֗וֹ אֶחָ֥ד מִפּ֛וֹ וְאֶחָ֥ד מִפּ֖וֹ אֶל־אילו [אֵילָֽיו׃]

i18n.en: And seven steps were its ascent, and its vestibules were before them; and it had palm-trees, one on this side and one on that side, on its posts.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, three readings: Ketiv *ʿlwtw* / Qere *ʿōlôṯāyw* 'its ascent'; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules'; Ketiv *ʾylw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw* 'its posts' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). The last stands at the end of the verse, and the source edition prints the sof pasuq inside the bracketed Qere; the text is kept as delivered. *ûmaʿălôṯ šiḇʿâ ʿōlôṯāyw* is rendered 'And seven steps were its ascent'.

paragraphs.text: וְשַׁ֛עַר לֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֑וֹם וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל־הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And there was a gate to the inner court toward the south; and he measured from gate to gate toward the south, a hundred cubits.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֛נִי אֶל־חָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖י בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַדָּר֑וֹם וַיָּ֙מָד֙ אֶת־הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַדָּר֔וֹם כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me into the inner court by the south gate, and he measured the south gate according to these measures;

notes.official: *wayḇîʾēnî ʾel-ḥăṣar happənîmî bəšaʿar haddārôm* 'Then he brought me into the inner court by the south gate'. The three inner gates (vv 28-37) mirror the outer ones but face outward, with their vestibules toward the outer court (vv 31, 34, 37).

paragraphs.text: ותאו [וְתָאָ֞יו] ואילו [וְאֵילָ֤יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙] כַּמִּדּ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְחַלּוֹנ֥וֹת ל֛וֹ ולאלמו [וּלְאֵלַמָּ֖יו] סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֕חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ אַמּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: and its guardrooms and its posts and its vestibules were according to these measures; and there were windows in it and in its vestibules all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, four readings: Ketiv *wtʾw* / Qere *wəṯāʾāyw*; Ketiv *wʾylw* / Qere *wəʾêlāyw*; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw*; Ketiv *wlʾlmw* / Qere *ûləʾêlammāyw* ('its guardrooms ... its posts ... its vestibules ... in its vestibules'; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵֽלַמּ֖וֹת סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב אֹ֗רֶךְ חָמֵ֤שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ אַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֖חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And there were vestibules all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.

notes.official: *wəʾêlammôṯ sāḇîḇ sāḇîḇ ʾōreḵ ḥāmēš wəʿeśrîm ʾammâ wərōḥaḇ ḥāmēš ʾammôṯ* 'And there were vestibules all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide'. The verse is absent in the LXX and some Hebrew manuscripts and is often explained as a dittography or a gloss. Its figures do not match the gate vestibule of v 9 (eight by two cubits), which is why the sense of the plural *ʾêlammôṯ* is disputed (`elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`). The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵלַמָּ֗ו אֶל־חָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣צוֹנָ֔ה וְתִמֹרִ֖ים אֶל־אילו [אֵילָ֑יו] וּמַעֲל֥וֹת שְׁמוֹנֶ֖ה מעלו [מַעֲלָֽיו׃]

i18n.en: And its vestibules were toward the outer court, and palm-trees were on its posts, and its ascent was eight steps.

notes.official: *wəʾêlammāw ʾel-ḥāṣēr haḥîṣōnâ* 'And its vestibules were toward the outer court' (`elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`). The form *ʾêlammāw* is written without a Ketiv. Ketiv/Qere, two readings: Ketiv *ʾylw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw* 'its posts'; Ketiv *mʿlw* / Qere *maʿălāyw* 'its ascent' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; the sof pasuq stands inside the bracket in the source). *ûšəmōnê maʿălôṯ* 'eight steps' up from the outer court to the inner.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֛נִי אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וַיָּ֣מָד אֶת־הַשַּׁ֔עַר כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me into the inner court toward the east, and he measured the gate according to these measures;

paragraphs.text: ותאו [וְתָאָ֞יו] ואלו [וְאֵלָ֤יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙] כַּמִּדּ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְחַלּוֹנ֥וֹת ל֛וֹ ולאלמו [וּלְאֵלַמָּ֖יו] סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב אֹ֚רֶךְ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: and its guardrooms and its posts and its vestibules were according to these measures; and there were windows in it and in its vestibules all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, four readings: Ketiv *wtʾw* / Qere *wəṯāʾāyw*; Ketiv *wʾlw* / Qere *wəʾêlāyw*; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw*; Ketiv *wlʾlmw* / Qere *ûləʾêlammāyw* (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: ואלמו [וְאֵלַמָּ֗יו] לֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה וְתִמֹרִ֥ים אֶל־אלו [אֵלָ֖יו] מִפּ֣וֹ וּמִפּ֑וֹ וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מַעֲל֖וֹת מעלו [מַעֲלָֽיו׃]

i18n.en: And its vestibules were toward the outer court, and palm-trees were on its posts on this side and on that side, and its ascent was eight steps.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, three readings: Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules'; Ketiv *ʾlw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw* 'its posts'; Ketiv *mʿlw* / Qere *maʿălāyw* 'its ascent' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל־שַׁ֣עַר הַצָּפ֑וֹן וּמָדַ֖ד כַּמִּדּ֥וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me to the north gate, and he measured it according to these measures:

paragraphs.text: תאו [תָּאָיו֙] אלו [אֵלָ֣יו] ואלמו [וְאֵֽלַמָּ֔יו] וְחַלּוֹנ֥וֹת ל֖וֹ סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב אֹ֚רֶךְ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: its guardrooms, its posts, and its vestibules; and there were windows in it all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere, three readings: Ketiv *tʾw* / Qere *tāʾāyw* 'its guardrooms'; Ketiv *ʾlw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw* 'its posts'; Ketiv *wʾlmw* / Qere *wəʾêlammāyw* 'and its vestibules' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`; `ta-guardroom-gate-chambers-ezekiel-40`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`; `elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40`).

paragraphs.text: ואילו [וְאֵילָ֗יו] לֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה וְתִמֹרִ֥ים אֶל־אילו [אֵילָ֖יו] מִפּ֣וֹ וּמִפּ֑וֹ וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מַעֲל֖וֹת מעלו [מַעֲלָֽיו׃]

i18n.en: And its posts were toward the outer court, and palm-trees were on its posts on this side and on that side, and its ascent was eight steps.

notes.official: *wəʾêlāyw ləḥāṣēr haḥîṣônâ* 'And its posts were toward the outer court'. At the parallel verses 31 and 34 the first word is 'its vestibules', and the LXX reads 'vestibules' here as well; the MT 'posts' is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; `ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`). Ketiv/Qere, three readings: Ketiv *wʾylw* / Qere *wəʾêlāyw*; Ketiv *ʾylw* / Qere *ʾêlāyw*; Ketiv *mʿlw* / Qere *maʿălāyw* (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וְלִשְׁכָּ֣ה וּפִתְחָ֔הּ בְּאֵילִ֖ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים שָׁ֖ם יָדִ֥יחוּ אֶת־הָעֹלָֽה׃

i18n.en: And there was a chamber with its entrance by the posts of the gates; there they would wash the burnt-offering.

notes.official: *wəlišəkâ ûp̄iṯḥāh bəʾêlîm haššəʿārîm* 'And there was a chamber with its entrance by the posts of the gates' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`). *šām yāḏîḥû ʾeṯ-hāʿōlâ* 'there they would wash the burnt-offering': *hēḏîaḥ* 'rinse' is used of washing the sacrificial parts (2 Chr 4:6) (`olah-burnt-offering`).

paragraphs.text: וּבְאֻלָ֣ם הַשַּׁ֗עַר שְׁנַ֤יִם שֻׁלְחָנוֹת֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וּשְׁנַ֥יִם שֻׁלְחָנ֖וֹת מִפֹּ֑ה לִשְׁח֤וֹט אֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָעוֹלָ֔ה וְהַחַטָּ֖את וְהָאָשָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And in the porch of the gate were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, on which to slaughter the burnt-offering and the sin-offering and the guilt-offering.

notes.official: *hāʿôlâ wəhaḥaṭṭāʾṯ wəhāʾāšām* 'the burnt-offering and the sin-offering and the guilt-offering'. The new central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus` governs the cultic vocabulary of chs. 40-46. *ḥaṭṭāʾṯ* keeps the traditional 'sin-offering'; Milgrom (*Leviticus 1-16*, AB 3, 1991) argues for 'purification offering'. For *ʾāšām* the modern 'guilt-offering' (NRSV, NJPS; isaiah-woh at Isa 53:10) replaces the ASV 'trespass-offering'; Milgrom's 'reparation offering' is noted. *ʾûlām haššaʿar* 'the porch of the gate' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`); `olah-burnt-offering`.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶל־הַכָּתֵ֣ף מִח֗וּצָה לָעוֹלֶה֙ לְפֶ֙תַח֙ הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַצָּפ֔וֹנָה שְׁנַ֖יִם שֻׁלְחָנ֑וֹת וְאֶל־הַכָּתֵ֣ף הָאַחֶ֗רֶת אֲשֶׁר֙ לְאֻלָ֣ם הַשַּׁ֔עַר שְׁנַ֖יִם שֻׁלְחָנֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And at the side outside, as one goes up to the entrance of the gate toward the north, were two tables; and at the other side, which belonged to the porch of the gate, were two tables.

notes.official: *ʾûlām haššaʿar* 'the porch of the gate' (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). The tables stand outside the north inner gate, two on each side of its entrance (cf. v 41).

paragraphs.text: אַרְבָּעָ֨ה שֻׁלְחָנ֜וֹת מִפֹּ֗ה וְאַרְבָּעָ֧ה שֻׁלְחָנ֛וֹת מִפֹּ֖ה לְכֶ֣תֶף הַשָּׁ֑עַר שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה שֻׁלְחָנ֖וֹת אֲלֵיהֶ֥ם יִשְׁחָֽטוּ׃

i18n.en: Four tables on this side and four tables on that side, at the side of the gate — eight tables, on which they would slaughter.

notes.official: *šəmōnâ šulḥānôṯ ʾălêhem yišḥāṭû* 'eight tables, on which they would slaughter': four inside the porch (v 39) and four outside it (v 40).

paragraphs.text: וְאַרְבָּעָה֩ שֻׁלְחָנ֨וֹת לָעוֹלָ֜ה אַבְנֵ֣י גָזִ֗ית אֹרֶךְ֩ אַמָּ֨ה אַחַ֤ת וָחֵ֙צִי֙ וְרֹ֨חַב אַמָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ וָחֵ֔צִי וְגֹ֖בַהּ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם וְיַנִּ֤יחוּ אֶת־הַכֵּלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁחֲט֧וּ אֶת־הָעוֹלָ֛ה בָּ֖ם וְהַזָּֽבַח׃

i18n.en: And four tables for the burnt-offering, of hewn stone, a cubit and a half long and a cubit and a half wide and one cubit high; on them they would lay the instruments with which they slaughtered the burnt-offering and the sacrifice.

notes.official: *ʾaḇnê ḡāzîṯ* 'hewn stone', dressed ashlar. *ʾeṯ-hāʿôlâ wəhazzāḇaḥ* 'the burnt-offering and the sacrifice' (`olah-burnt-offering`): *zeḇaḥ* is the slaughtered sacrifice eaten by the worshippers (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַֽשְׁפַתַּ֗יִם טֹ֧פַח אֶחָ֛ד מוּכָנִ֥ים בַּבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב וְאֶל־הַשֻּׁלְחָנ֖וֹת בְּשַׂ֥ר הַקָּרְבָֽן׃

i18n.en: And the hooks, one handbreadth, were fastened in the house all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering.

notes.official: *wəhaššəp̄attayim ṭōp̄aḥ ʾeḥāḏ mûḵānîm babbayiṯ* 'And the hooks, one handbreadth, were fastened in the house'. *šəp̄attayim* is a dual whose other use (Ps 68:14 [ET 68:13]) is usually taken as 'sheepfolds' or 'hearth-stones'. The ASV has 'hooks' and NRSV 'pegs'; the LXX and others take it as a hand-wide ledge or rim around the tables. The ASV is kept. *bəśar haqqorbān* 'the flesh of the offering': *qorbān* ('what is brought near') is rendered 'offering' so that it stays apart from *tərûmâ*, which keeps the ASV 'oblation' (44:30) (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וּמִחוּצָה֩ לַשַּׁ֨עַר הַפְּנִימִ֜י לִֽשְׁכ֣וֹת שָׁרִ֗ים בֶּחָצֵ֤ר הַפְּנִימִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֗ר אֶל־כֶּ֙תֶף֙ שַׁ֣עַר הַצָּפ֔וֹן וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֑וֹם אֶחָ֗ד אֶל־כֶּ֙תֶף֙ שַׁ֣עַר הַקָּדִ֔ים פְּנֵ֖י דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַצָּפֹֽן׃

i18n.en: And outside the inner gate were chambers for the singers in the inner court, which was beside the north gate, with their faces toward the south; one was beside the east gate, facing toward the north.

notes.official: *lišḵôṯ šārîm* 'chambers for the singers' and 'beside the east gate' are the MT. The LXX reads 'two chambers' (*šəttayim*) and 'the south gate', which agrees with vv 45-46 (two priests' chambers, one facing south and one facing north). NRSV follows the LXX. The MT is translated, as in the ASV (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלָ֑י זֹ֣ה הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנֶ֙יהָ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם לַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "This chamber whose face is toward the south is for the priests who keep the charge of the house;

notes.official: The man's speech (40:45-46). *šōmərê mišmereṯ habbayiṯ* 'who keep the charge of the house': *šāmar mišmereṯ* is the Priestly idiom for guard duty and service (Num 3:7-8, 28, 32, 38), used again in 44:8, 14-16.

paragraphs.text: וְהַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנֶ֙יהָ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן לַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים שֹׁמְרֵ֖י מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ הֵ֣מָּה בְנֵֽי־צָד֗וֹק הַקְּרֵבִ֧ים מִבְּנֵֽי־לֵוִ֛י אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לְשָׁרְתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: and the chamber whose face is toward the north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who from among the sons of Levi come near to YHWH to minister to him."

notes.official: *hēmmâ ḇənê-ṣāḏôq haqqərēḇîm mibbənê-lēwî ʾel-YHWH ləšārəṯô* 'These are the sons of Zadok, who from among the sons of Levi come near to YHWH to minister to him'. This is the first statement of the Zadokite privilege developed in 43:19 and 44:15-16. *qārēḇ* 'come near' is the technical verb of priestly access (Lev 10:3; Num 16:5). Names are in their English forms (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֨מָד אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֜ר אֹ֣רֶךְ ׀ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֛חַב מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה מְרֻבָּ֑עַת וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: He measured the court, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, square; and the altar was before the house.

notes.official: *mərubbāʿaṯ* 'square': the inner court is a hundred-cubit square, with the altar (43:13-17) at its centre, before the house.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל־אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ וַיָּ֙מָד֙ אֵ֣ל אֻלָ֔ם חָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפֹּ֔ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפֹּ֑ה וְרֹ֣חַב הַשַּׁ֔עַר שָׁלֹ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Then he brought me to the porch of the house and measured the post of the porch, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side; and the width of the gate, three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.

notes.official: *ʾûlām habbayiṯ* 'the porch of the house', the ʾûlām of the Temple building itself, as in 1 Kgs 6:3 (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *ʾēl ʾūlām* 'the post of the porch' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`). The LXX gives the width of the porch doorway ('fourteen cubits') before 'three cubits on this side'. That figure is not in the MT, which is translated as it stands (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`).

paragraphs.text: אֹ֣רֶךְ הָאֻלָ֞ם עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֙חַב֙ עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אַמָּ֔ה וּבַֽמַּעֲל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲל֖וּ אֵלָ֑יו וְעַמֻּדִים֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֵילִ֔ים אֶחָ֥ד מִפֹּ֖ה וְאֶחָ֥ד מִפֹּֽה׃

i18n.en: The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits, and by the steps by which they would go up to it; and there were pillars by the posts, one on this side and one on that side.

notes.official: *ʾōreḵ hāʾûlām ʿeśrîm ʾammâ wərōḥaḇ ʿaštê ʿeśrēh ʾammâ* 'The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits': the LXX has 'twelve' (as 1 Kgs 6:3 has ten for the breadth). *ûḇammaʿălôṯ ʾăšer yaʿălû ʾēlāyw* 'and by the steps by which they would go up to it' is elliptical in the MT, where the LXX has 'ten steps'. The MT is translated and the ellipsis left (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *wəʿammûḏîm ʾel-hāʾêlîm* 'and there were pillars by the posts': *ʿammûḏ* 'pillar' is kept apart from *ʾayil* 'post' (`ayil-post-architectural-pier-ezekiel-40`). The pillars recall Yakhin and Boaz (1 Kgs 7:15-22).
